Issued at 334 AM CDT Tue Sep 8 2026

Morning Showers and Storms:

A line of showers and thunderstorms seen moving east across 
Minnesota into North Central Wisconsin on RADAR imagery will
continue to develop along the nose of the low level jet as it 
drifts east through the Upper Midwest. As these storms start to
move in later this morning, a few of these could be marginally 
string to severe. There will be some elevated instability on the
order of 500-1000 J/kg to tap into with 25-35 kts of cloud 
layer shear. The strongest cores may be able to produce some 
marginally severe hail and a few strong wind gusts.

Additional Storm Potential Today:

Activity is expected to dwindle into the late morning/afternoon
as the low level jet weakens and veers with time and low level 
forcing becomes a bit more nebulous across the region. Southerly
return flow and a fairly stout axis of 850 mb moisture 
transport will continue to push into the region, allowing for 
pWats to climb upwards of 2 inches by the afternoon. As 
afternoon turns into evening, upper level support looks to 
improve slightly with a shortwave impulse moving through the 
building jet on the lee side of the trough axis. A reinvigoration
of showers and storms along and ahead of the cold front is 
expected, again on the zone of a building low level jet. This 
should mainly be south of the Minnesota state line in Iowa and 
Wisconsin. 

A low, albeit slightly higher than the morning storms, potential
(5-15%) for strong to severe storms with this activity as 
instability will be weak (no more than 1000 J/kg) with generally
less than 30 kts of effective shear across the region. DCAPE 
values between 750-900 J/kg results in strong/damaging wind 
gusts as the main severe concern within the strongest cores. 

The overall progressive nature of the front across our area 
should limit the flooding threat but some higher totals may be 
possible for our Northeast Iowa counties as the front looks to 
have a bit slower forward motion there so storms may train a 
little longer. The HREF 07.12 and NBM 08.01 show vastly 
different stories as to probabilities for 1 inch of rain with 
the latter being much more bullish on precipitation (as it has 
been for the last couple of days). Given the pWats, the warm 
cloud depths, and overall favorable warm rain processes, would 
tend to lean more with the NBM on this occasion but much will 
depend on the overall coverage of storms in the evening. The 
front will continue to push through during the overnight hours 
with most outside of far Southwest Wisconsin seeing dry 
conditions by 12Z Wednesday. 

Wednesday - Thursday: Drying Out, Near Normal Temperatures

As the front pushes through the area, a noticeably drier airmass 
will follow in its wake. A weak high surface high will drop into the 
Western Great Lakes region and help keep the area dry for the mid to 
late week timeframe. In the upper levels, zonal flow to weak ridging 
will prevail so while a "cold front" will have moved through, 
temperatures will still be near normal in the 70s to low 80s. That 
being said, the decreased humidity should make somewhat of a 
difference.

Friday - This Weekend: Rain Chances Return, Cooler Temps? 

Moving towards the weekend, yet another upper trough looks to dig 
into the Upper Midwest, bringing with it another potential round of 
precipitation Friday night into Saturday. The 07.12 LREF Grand 
ensemble (GEFS/EC/GEPS) is already enthused about the potential for 
precipitation with probabilities in the 50-70% range for Friday 
night into Saturday. Given the upper trough and likelihood of a 
trailing cold front to be moving through around that time, along 
with strong return flow during the day on Friday, the chances for 
rain are looking pretty strong to start the weekend. Temperatures 
also look to take a bit of a hit as we potentially move into 
zonal/weakly northwest flow aloft. By Sunday, high temperatures may 
only be in the upper 60s to low 70s - much more reminiscent of the 
supposed meteorological fall we're in currently. The cooler 
temperatures could linger into mid next week as yet another system 
brings more modest chances for rain but there's still much that 
could change in regards to that this far out so will continue with 
the blended forecast solution at this time.
